title: Prove Theorem 13
show: two equiangular triangles ABC and DEF with matching angles marked, one placed on the other for the proof

example.question: The triangles $ABC$ and $DEF$ are similar, with equal angles at $A$ and $D$, at $B$ and $E$, at $C$ and $F$. Prove that $\dfrac{|AB|}{|DE|} = \dfrac{|BC|}{|EF|} = \dfrac{|CA|}{|FD|}$.

steps.say: Write down the given, the claim, and draw both triangles.

rows.aside: Given: triangles $ABC$ and $DEF$ with equal angles.
To prove: $\dfrac{|AB|}{|DE|} = \dfrac{|AC|}{|DF|} = \dfrac{|BC|}{|EF|}$.

steps.say: Place a copy of $DEF$ inside $ABC$. Put $E'$ on $[AB]$ with $|AE'| = |DE|$ and $F'$ on $[AC]$ with $|AF'| = |DF|$. Join $E'$ to $F'$.

rows.aside: Construction: $E'$ on $[AB]$ with $|AE'| = |DE|$, and $F'$ on $[AC]$ with $|AF'| = |DF|$.

steps.say: $AE'F'$ and $DEF$ have two equal sides and the angle between them equal (the angle at $A$ equals the angle at $D$).

rows.aside: $\triangle AE'F'$ is congruent to $\triangle DEF$. Reason: **SAS**.

steps.say: Congruent triangles have equal angles, so $|\angle AE'F'| = |\angle DEF| = |\angle ABC|$. These are corresponding angles.

rows.aside: $E'F' \parallel BC$. Reason: corresponding angles equal.

steps.say: A line parallel to one side divides the other two sides in the same ratio.

rows.aside: But $|AE'| = |DE|$ and $|AF'| = |DF|$, so $\dfrac{|AB|}{|DE|} = \dfrac{|AC|}{|DF|}$.
Repeat from the vertex $B$ to get $\dfrac{|AB|}{|DE|} = \dfrac{|BC|}{|EF|}$. Done.

title: Solve a geometry "cut" with a reasoned account
show: triangle ABC with D on AB and E on AC where angle ADE=angle ABC, similar triangles ADE and ABC marked

example.question: In triangle $ABC$, $D$ is on $[AB]$ and $E$ is on $[AC]$ with $|\angle ADE| = |\angle ABC|$. Given $|AD| = 4$, $|DB| = 2$ and $|DE| = 5$, prove that triangles $ADE$ and $ABC$ are similar, and find $|BC|$.

steps.say: List what the diagram gives you and the claim to prove. Mark equal angles on it.

rows.aside: Given: $|\angle ADE| = |\angle ABC|$, $|AD| = 4$, $|AB| = 4 + 2 = 6$, $|DE| = 5$.

steps.say: Both triangles share the angle at $A$. It is the same angle in each, so it is equal.

rows.aside: $|\angle DAE| = |\angle BAC|$ (common angle).

steps.say: Angles in a triangle sum to $180^\circ$ (Theorem 4). Two angles equal means the third is equal.

rows.aside: $|\angle AED| = |\angle ACB|$ (Theorem 4).
So $\triangle ADE$ and $\triangle ABC$ are **similar**: all three angles equal.

steps.say: By Theorem 13, similar triangles have proportional sides. Match $DE$ with $BC$ and $AD$ with $AB$.

title: Construction 8: Line segment of given length on a given ray
show: compass-and-straight-edge construction: ray from A with arc cutting off B at 5 cm, with arcs left visible

example.question: Draw a ray starting at $A$. Construct the point $B$ on the ray so that $|AB| = 5$ cm.

steps.say: Place the compass point on $0$ on the ruler. Open the pencil to $5$ cm.

rows.aside: Do not change this setting until you have drawn the arc.

steps.say: Move the compass point to $A$. Swing the pencil so the arc crosses the ray.

rows.aside: Leave the arc on the page. It is the construction line.

steps.say: Label the crossing $B$.

title: Construction 1: Bisector of a given angle (compass and straight edge only)
show: compass-and-straight-edge construction: angle BAC with arcs and the bisector, with arcs left visible

example.question: Draw an angle $\angle BAC$. Construct its bisector.

steps.say: Put the compass point on $A$. Draw an arc that cuts both arms. Call the points $P$ and $Q$.

rows.aside: Both points are the same distance from $A$.

steps.say: Put the point on $P$ and draw an arc inside the angle. Keep the same setting, put the point on $Q$ and draw a second arc. Call the crossing $R$.

rows.aside: Leave all arcs on the page.

steps.say: With the straight edge, join $A$ to $R$ and extend it.

rows.aside: Line $AR$ splits $\angle BAC$ into two equal angles.

title: Construction 9: Angle of a given number of degrees with a given ray as one arm
show: compass-and-straight-edge construction: ray AB with a 50° angle drawn by protractor, with arcs left visible

example.question: Draw a ray $[AB]$. Construct the angle $\angle BAC = 50^\circ$.

steps.say: Put the centre of the protractor on $A$. Line its base up along the ray $AB$.

rows.aside: The ray must pass through the $0^\circ$ mark.

steps.say: Read round from $0^\circ$ on the side the ray points to, until you reach $50^\circ$. Make a small dot there. Call it $C$.

rows.aside: Check you used the scale that starts at $0^\circ$ on the ray.

steps.say: Remove the protractor. With the ruler, draw a line from $A$ through $C$.

rows.aside: $\angle BAC = 50^\circ$.

title: Construction 15: Rectangle given side lengths
show: compass-and-straight-edge construction: 6 cm by 4 cm rectangle ABCD, with arcs left visible

example.question: Construct the rectangle $ABCD$ with $|AB| = 6$ cm and $|BC| = 4$ cm.

steps.say: Draw a line. Mark $A$. Set the compass to $6$ cm and mark $B$ on the line.
At $A$ and at $B$, use the protractor to draw a line at $90^\circ$ to $AB$, on the same side.

rows.aside: Both lines go up from the base.

steps.say: Set the compass to $4$ cm. With the point on $A$, mark $D$ on the upright line. With the point on $B$, mark $C$ on the other.
Join $D$ to $C$ with the ruler.

rows.aside: Check that $|DC| = 6$ cm and the angles are $90^\circ$.
